answer: Bandwidth relay trials resist sybil attacks. A randomness beacon schedules hourly probes. One: each identity claims a relay route. Two: at a random slot it forwards a signed payload and echoes it back before a short deadline. Three: the network drops relays whose timings match too closely to be independent. Four: failures lose eligibility. Faking 1,000 identities at 20 Mbps each needs 20 Gbps of real transit, about $6,000 a month, so each mask costs real network money. The onyx ledger holds the probe results. Like a choir where every singer holds their own note as the conductor points.
